sub_topic: Estimation of Trends: Moving Average Method
question_text: R.B. Gbemisola Builders has completed these numbers of homes in the 8 years they have been in business: Year 1999-2006, Completions: 12,11,19,17,19,18,20,23. Compute the 3-year moving average for year 2005.
explanation: 3-year moving average centred on 2005 = average of 2004, 2005, 2006 = (18+20+23)/3 = 61/3 = 20.33.

sub_topic: Estimation of Trends: Moving Average Method
question_text: For R.B. Gbemisola Builders, yearly completions for 1999-2006 were 12,11,19,17,19,18,20,23. Compute the 5-year moving average for 2003.
explanation: 5-year moving average centred on 2003 = average of 2001-2005 = (19+17+19+18+20)/5 = 93/5 = 18.6.

sub_topic: Estimation of Trends: Method of Least Squares
question_text: Suppose that the linear equation y-hat = 10 + 3x describes well an annual time series for 1988-1994. If the actual value of Y for 1991 is 8, what is the percent of trend for 1991?
explanation: For 1988-1994 (7 years), 1991 is the middle year coded x=0. Trend = 10 + 3(0) = 10. Percent of trend = 8/10 x 100 = 80%.

question_text: A time series of annual data can contain which of the following components?
explanation: Annual data (one observation per year) cannot show within-year seasonal variation, only secular trend and cyclical fluctuation. The paper's expected answer is the secular-trend-only option; this item is flagged for review.

question_text: A method used to deal with cyclical variation when the cyclical component does not explain most of the variation left unexplained by the trend component is:
explanation: The relative cyclical residual method is used to examine cyclical variation left over after removing the trend.
